message.content:
Now I understand the TLV format. The TLV_RAW is 6 bytes: 2 bytes for type (little-endian) and 4 bytes for length (little-endian).

Now let me understand the vulnerability trigger better. The key issue is:
1. `response_index` starts at 1
2. When a response is sent, `response_index` is incremented
3. The check `if(sman->response_index > TLV_MAX_NUM_RESPONSES || sman->responses[sman->response_index].data == NULL)` - when `response_index == 11`, the first condition `> 11` is false, so it accesses `responses[11]` which is out of bounds (array has indices 0-10).

So I need to set up 11 responses (indices 0-10) for `sockman[0]`, and then have the fuzzer send all 11 responses. When it tries to send the 12th response (index 11), it will access `responses[11]` which is out of bounds.

Wait, let me re-read the code more carefully:

```c
sman->response_index++;
if(sman->response_index > TLV_MAX_NUM_RESPONSES ||
   sman->responses[sman->response_index].data == NULL) {
```

So after sending response at index `response_index`, it increments. If `response_index` becomes 11, the check `11 > 11` is false, so it evaluates `sman->responses[11].data` which is out of bounds.

But wait - the check happens AFTER the response is sent. So the sequence is:
1. `response_index = 1`, send `responses[1]`, increment to 2
2. Check `2 > 11`? No. Check `responses[2].data == NULL`? If not NULL, continue
3. ... and so on
4. `response_index = 10`, send `responses[10]`, increment to 11
5. Check `11 > 11`? No. Check `responses[11].data == NULL`? This is out of bounds!

So I need to set up responses 0-10 (all 11 responses) for `sockman[0]`, and have the fuzzer send all of them. The 12th send attempt (when `response_index` becomes 11) will trigger the OOB read.

But wait - I also need to understand how the fuzzer actually sends responses. Looking at the code:
- `response_index` starts at 1
- Response 0 is sent when the socket is connected (as mentioned in the comment)
- Responses 1-10 are sent when the socket becomes readable

Let me look at how response 0 is sent and how the socket connection works.
